name: 128. OpenAI Fast service tier bills at Fast rates and is echoed to the client (fast-service-tier)
description:
OpenAI renamed Priority processing to Fast mode on 2026-07-30 (service_tier "fast"; "priority" still accepted) and bills it at 2x Standard.
The datasheet stores those rates under the _priority columns. Before the fix, tierFromResponse only matched priority/flex/ultrafast, so a
served "fast" response billed at Standard (a customer gpt-6-astra call logged $0.00886 instead of $0.01772), and
BifrostResponsesResponse.WithDefaults rewrote the unknown tier to "auto" on /v1/responses.

128.1/128.2 pin /v1/responses (non-streaming and streaming): the echoed service_tier is fast (or default when OpenAI downgraded, which OpenAI also bills at Standard), never auto.
128.3 pins /v1/chat/completions. All three send x-bf-expect-cost so the dbverify reporter recomputes the logged cost from the datasheet at the
served tier (fast -> _priority columns) and fails on a Standard-rate charge. x-bf-send-back-raw-request proves service_tier fast left for OpenAI unchanged.
Prompts are tiny and uncached so Fast cost is exactly 2x Standard for the row tokens.
